Video poem and installation by Giacomo Marinsalta
Music by Lola Lextrait

Can an everyday gesture and an ordinary object like laundry—typically excluded from the aesthetic gaze—reveal their own form of beauty?

The words of a poem accompany a life suspended between dream and reality, in a journey made of images of sheets and clothes hanging in the wind along the streets of a Mediterranean city. 

The evocative image of laundry blurs the boundaries between inside and outside, public and private. Through narrow alleys, balconies, and windows, the fabrics are transformed into language, architectural ornament, and a symbol of care and resistance, in contrast with an urban policy increasingly dominated by the aesthetics of decorum.

The project takes shape from the thesis research for the Master of Arts in European Media Studies at the University of Potsdam, entitled “Laundering Dreams in the Porous City – The Political Aesthetics of Laundry in Public Space.”

Curation, communication and graphic design for the solo exhibition Bestiario Prossimo by Cesare D’Antonio, a set designer and multifaceted artist based in San Benedetto del Tronto, Le Marche, Italy.
The exhibition presented an exploration of the bond between humanity and the animal kingdom, unfolding through a variety of artistic techniques, including paintings, prints, ceramics and installations. 
Each work invited the visitor to reflect on the intrinsic value of animals, not only as companions, but as beings endowed with their own dignity and wisdom.

Drawing on the concepts of astrology and grounded in real climate science, Climate Fortunes is a web app that offers a glimpse into a future that is more certain than we might wish. 
Developed during the Environmental Data, Media, and the Humanities Hackathon held from May 31 to June 2, 2023, in Potsdam, this project was organized by the Network of Digital Humanities at the University of Potsdam, in collaboration with Lukas Diestel, Maximilian Hepach, Giacomo Marinsalta, Sybille Neumeyer, Jonas Parnow, Birgit Schneider, and May Ee Wong. The initiative was funded by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, and the source code is available on GitHub.

Wicked Games – For a morphology of gestures

Wicked Games For a Morphology of Gestures Featured in Queerpandemia – Contaminazioni artistische di altro genere (Tlon 2024), Wicked Games – For a Morphology of Gestures presents an artwork series, in which movement is represented as spasmodic response of the body to the pervasiveness of digitization. During the pandemic the invisible agent of the virus has […]

Featured in Queerpandemia – Contaminazioni artistische di altro genere (Tlon 2024), Wicked Games – For a Morphology of Gestures presents an artwork series, in which movement is represented as spasmodic response of the body to the pervasiveness of digitization.
During the pandemic the invisible agent of the virus has exacerbated a fear intimately connected to bodies, projecting the possibility of death into media and news. A cosmic void serves behind our gestures as the backdrop to a feeling of meaninglessness we all felt somehow during this time.
The impoverishment of the meaning of images dictated by their constant consumption, in a continuous virtual flow, has led to an artistic contemplation of the physical qualities of the mineral world, whose incredibly slow crystalline transformations remain on the contrary imperceptible to human scrutiny. These creations occur over millennia through inconspicuous changes in accidental terrestrial conditions. The natural phenomena of material change affecting minerals create evocative forms and signs, capturing the human eye. Hands move randomly to the glitched impression of the machine. Skin is joined by stone as an excrescence of the world, with textures interweaving with objects and their appearances, in the rhythm of a common cosmic becoming.

The Offener Kanal Europa explored the neighbourhood of Alexanderplatz in 2022 as part of the Open Call gemainsam um die Häuser ziehen launched by the Haus of Statistik.
The duo formed by Nora Spiekermann and Giacomo Marinsalta asked: What is it like to live right at Alexanderplatz? Do people know about the House of Statistics? What value does the project hold for the city centre?
Their research led to the creation of a large live broadcast on the street in front of the Haus of Statistics, as well as an interview series with 6 episodes under the title Alles Anders TV, followed by two performative tours in the neighborhood.

Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis

Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis is a video installation featuring an experimental film on the 2022 World Exposition in Dubai. The film draws inspiration from Plato’s myth of the lost island empire of Atlantis, which sank undersea at the peak of its civilization and […]

Excuse Us While We Improve Your View, Atlantis is a video installation featuring an experimental film on the 2022 World Exposition in Dubai.
The film draws inspiration from Plato’s myth of the lost island empire of Atlantis, which sank undersea at the peak of its civilization and ideal state power. The installation translates Atlantis’ mythical imagery into the aesthetics of Dubai’s international free trade zones, luxury real estate, and World Exposition sightseeing, symbolizing new social orders and frontiers for state-of-the-art cosmopolitan urbanism. Through a blend of commercial spots and personal travel recordings capturing a journey through the metropolis until the Expo’s venue, the visual research documents the world representation mediated by Expo – a “worldling” – blurring the line between reality and fiction.
Atlantis becomes a legendary tourist destination, reflecting a Western tendency to romanticize and exoticize faraway lands, perpetuating an othering and voyeuristic gaze, allured by the realization of an unknown elsewhere. The narrative unfolds within a surveilled, enclosed, and transient fair, where political expression is marginalized. Passports transform into branded gadgets, serving as symbols of manufactured global contact, creating an illusion of an external reality with equal freedom of movement for all.
Immersive experiences, idealistic rhetoric on sustainability, and promises of “real-world” solutions simulate a worldly narrative, enchanting virtual visitors and passenger spectators alike. Whether envisioned as a utopian „island of the blessed,“ an oasis amidst the desert, or a distant land on the horizon of the sea, Atlantis remains a mirage, an elusive vision of progress woven with nationalist dreams, an incessant stream of virtual landscapes, whose ‘concrete’ realization continually seeks to be improved and perfected.
Music by Aïna Spencer
Excuse Us While We Improve Your View Atlantis was exhibited in the conference “Un/Reale Interaktionsräume” funded by the program „Digital Realities“ by ZEM, in November 2022 at the FH Potsdam.

Stemmed out of ongoing conversations and personal thoughts shared since the spring of 2020, Cheerful Weaves – Labor für gelungene Abhängigkeiten (Laboratory for Joyful Dependencies) framed a self-organised process to reflect and experiment with collective practices of care. In the midst of the pandemic’s unfolding, intimate exchanges between friends waked a joyful militant wish to explore and acknowledge what mutual responsibilities and needs we share in caring for, with, of, and about each other, while holding together in a critical stance towards structures of power and dominance overarching society. 
Cheerful Weaves took place the 12-19 September 2021 at Libken e.V.
Residency program with artists invited for the week (Olga Golde, Ronald Berger, Giulia Claudia Massacci, Marina Prados, Paula Knüpling, Katrin Fisher).
In collaboration with Libken e.V. and Paula Becker, Louis Mauff, Kim Sanou.

Offener Kanal Europa is a media platform and intervention series based in public spaces initiated by Nora Spiekermann. Active in Berlin since 2020, it documents the profound changes caused by the financialization of urban spaces, particularly through real estate privatization, using interviews and street-level actions.

 

Logo, Graphic & Web Design, Performance Art, Video, Curation
More Info: Offener Kanal Europa
 
Offener Kanal Europa took over a former Imbiss in the summer of 2020, located in the privatized neighborhood of Europacity in Berlin. Designed in the shape of a birdhouse, it served as a studio for a mobile TV channel and hosted various events. The first series of interviews posed questions such as:

What moves Europacity?
What should the neighborhood look like in the future?
How is public space changing?

Die Stadt als Papier Denken
Performance in Public Space

To celebrate the publishing of the fanzine Lothars Reise the Offener Kanal Europa organized in August 2021 an artistic performance in public space titled Die Stadt als Papier Denken.
Through a mobile DYI station the performance saw passerbies of the streets of Europacity, Berlin cutting and folding the zines.

Lothars Letzte Reise tells the story of a old neighbor of Wedding visiting for the first time the district of Europacity. Old and new contrasts emerge in what used to be and what will become the city. The fanzine was published by ZNAAACKS.
